newsitem.title: USA: Lufthansa aims to increase cargo flown to JFK.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa aims to increase cargo flown to JFK.

text.p: Lufthansa Cargo this year is looking to increase on the near 105,000 tonnes it flew to New York in 1996, its chairman Wilhelm Althem said.

"Not only has it (the Boeing 747 Freighter) helped propel Lufthansa cargo into market leadership, but it has also left an indelible mark on the history of modern aviation," Althem said at the 25th anniversary of the first Boeing 747F on Wednesday at JFK International Airport

To mark the 747's inaugural flight from Frankfurt to New York on April 19, 1972 Irene Halligan, the Commissioner of New York City, took part in a naming of a current 747 in honour of the City of New York, the carrier's most important North American gateway.
It is the first time Lufthansa has named an aircraft in honour of a city outside Germany, a Lufthansa statement said.

"Lufthansa Cargo is proud to have been the launch customer of the Boeing 747 Freighter," said Althen noting that the tonnage flown to New York last year surpassed any other carrier. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel +44 171 542 7706 Fax +5017
